dodo.accepted.caveat: Eligibility is decided by the country that issued your government ID (every director/owner for companies).

dodo.grandfathered.caveat: Only merchants already onboarded before the country was prohibited may continue (enhanced monitoring); no new sign-ups.

etsy.eligible.caveat: Countries marked * on Etsy's page accept Etsy Payments through a Payoneer Payment Account.

gplay.merchant_registration.caveat: Merchant registration is required to sell paid apps, in-app purchases or subscriptions.

lemon.bank_payouts.caveat: PayPal payouts are documented separately ('200+ countries' per PayPal's list) and are not confirmed per country here. Lemon Squeezy is migrating merchants to Stripe Managed Payments.

paddle.unsupported.caveat: Paddle states it 'works with software businesses anywhere in the world with the exception of' these countries. Software only; every seller and product is reviewed before sales are enabled.

paypal_payouts.eligible.caveat: PayPal Payouts is how many platforms (e.g. creator platforms) send earnings to PayPal accounts. A country missing here may still have PayPal accounts that can buy or send.

paypal_worldwide.markets.caveat: Listed = PayPal operates a site for this market. It does NOT say whether accounts there can receive money.

polar.payouts.caveat: Payouts run on Stripe Connect Express; individuals need Stripe Express to support the 'individual' business type in your country (check per Polar's FAQ).

upwork.restricted.caveat: Upwork: 'We support a thriving network of global freelancers in over 180 countries, but we're not available everywhere.' Also excluded: Crimea, DPR, LPR, individual nationals of Cuba, SDN-listed persons, and 'any other country or region restricted by law (this changes occasionally)'. Hand-curated from the help article (not an automated collector).

whop.payouts.caveat: Payout methods (bank, PayPal, crypto) vary by country and are shown in your Whop balance screen.

youtube_ypp.signup_areas.caveat: Availability is by the channel's country. The page also carries a 10 March 2022 note pausing new Russian AdSense/AdMob/Ad Manager accounts.

P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but under CEMAC exchange control (Regulation 02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM). Service-export receipts must be collected and repatriated by the exporter through its domiciliary bank via the BEAC (art. 70). Service transactions of FCFA 5m or more must be domiciled with a CEMAC credit institution (art. 68) and backed by a contract, purchase order or invoice (art. 69). Foreign currency received by banks is surrendered to the BEAC.

sources.publisher: BEAC — Règlement n°02/18/CEMAC/UMAC/CM portant réglementation des changes
sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 70
sources.quote: Article 70. Les recettes d'exportation des services sont recouvrées et rapatriées par I'exportateur à travers sa banque domiciliataire par I'entremise de la Banque Centrale.

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 68
sources.quote: Article 68. Les transactions avec I'extérieur liées aux services d'un montant égal ou supérieur à 5 millions de Francs CFA sont domiciliées auprès d'un établissement de crédit de la CEMAC.

P1_fx_receipts.notes: OCR text of the BEAC PDF (e.g. 'I'extérieur'); quotes copied as extracted. No specific repatriation deadline for services found (goods: 150 days). Later BEAC instructions not checked. Applies in all six CEMAC states.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: No. Opening a foreign-currency account within CEMAC for a resident is not authorised (art. 43). Only resident legal persons may be authorised by the BEAC. Resident individuals' accounts abroad must be declared to the BEAC (art. 42).

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 43
sources.quote: Article 43. L'ouverture d'un compte en devises dans la CEMAC au profit d'un résident n'est pas autorisée.

sources.title: Règlement 02/18/CEMAC, art. 42
sources.quote: Article 42. Les comptes des personnes physiques résidentes ouverts à l'étranger sont déclarés à la Banque Centrale.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Cameroon (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Whop (payouts); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Lemon Squeezy payouts; Polar (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: Effectively no for income. A Cameroonian PayPal account can receive payments, but per a 2026 guide the balance can only be used for online payments, and users cannot withdraw to local bank accounts. Cameroon is not on the PayPal Payouts list.

P5_payoneer_wise.question: Payoneer / Wise availability for residents
P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Wise: Cameroon is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money. Payoneer: not confirmed (only forum/blog testimony). Under CEMAC rules, individuals must declare foreign accounts to the BEAC (P2).

sources.title: Where do I need to live to hold money with Wise?
sources.quote: The complete list of countries/territories whose residents can hold money (Andorra ... Uruguay) does not include Cameroon.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: an individual enterprise (entreprenant/sole trader) registered at the CFCE one-stop shop, which handles RCCM and NIU. A commercial guide estimates FCFA 46,500 (5,000 name reservation + 41,500 RCCM) and about 5 days, with no notary needed.
L1_registration.note: Only commercial guides (Kolonell) captured for CFCE costs/steps; CFCE's own site not consulted on 2026-10-21.

sources.title: Créer son entreprise au Cameroun (2026) — CFCE
sources.quote: Les étapes au Cameroun via le CFCE Le CFCE est un guichet unique qui regroupe l'immatriculation au registre du commerce, l'obtention du numéro d'identifiant unique (NIU) fiscal, et les déclarations sociales.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The NIU (Numéro d'Identifiant Unique), a 14-character taxpayer number from the DGI. Since April 2025 registration is online-only via the DGI tele-declaration platform, using the national ID card number. Since Finance Law 2020 it has been required to open a bank account, connect utilities, take out insurance, and for other transactions.

sources.quote: Procédure pour obtenir le NIU en ligne Depuis avril 2025, l’immatriculation fiscale s’effectue exclusivement en ligne via la plateforme officielle de télédéclaration de la DGI.

sources.title: Numéro identifiant fiscal Cameroun (NIU) : format, obtention, vérification
sources.quote: Au Cameroun, il s'appelle NIU (Numéro d'Identifiant Unique) et obéit à un format strict de 14 caractères qui révèle plusieurs informations sur le contribuable.

L2_tax_id.notes: Whether a FCFA 1,000 digital stamp applies is disputed between guides.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Since fiscal year 2025, the Impôt Général Synthétique (IGS) applies to businesses with turnover up to FCFA 50m. It replaced the impôt libératoire, the simplified regime, the business licence, VAT and personal income tax on commercial profits with a fixed annual amount per turnover class, paid quarterly to municipalities. Since January 2026, approved clients withhold 2% (5% for public procurement) on invoices, creditable only against the next year's IGS. Above FCFA 50m the real regime applies. Treatment of foreign-source income was not established.

sources.title: Le nouvel impôt IGS du Cameroun (22 Sep 2026)
sources.quote: Il regroupe plusieurs anciennes obligations — l'impôt libératoire, le régime simplifié, la patente, la TVA et l'impôt sur le revenu des personnes physiques frappant les bénéfices commerciaux — en un seul impôt forfaitaire unique pour les petites entreprises.

sources.title: IGS : retenue à la source de 2 % (2026)
sources.quote: Dans la même salle, la Chambre de commerce, d'industrie, des mines et de l'artisanat (CCIMA) a soulevé un problème que peu de dirigeants ont encore identifié dans leurs comptes : depuis janvier 2026, les clients habilités retiennent 2 % du montant hors taxes de vos factures — 5 % pour la commande publique — et ces retenues ne s'imputent que sur l'IGS de l'année suivante .

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: TRAP: some 2026 guides (incl. Lefisk's VAT page) still describe a 'régime simplifié' for FCFA 10–50m, which IGS replaced from FY2025. IGS class amounts not captured; CGI not read.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 19.25% effective (17.5% plus 10% municipal surcharge). Exports are zero-rated with VAT credit refunds. IGS taxpayers (turnover up to FCFA 50m) do not charge VAT. Whether online services to foreign clients qualify as exports was not confirmed against the CGI.
L4_vat_gst.note: Only one secondary domain captured (Lefisk VAT page; Kintsugi/PayPro results not captured); impots.cm CGI not retrieved on 2026-10-21.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 2024/017 of 23 Dec 2024 on personal data protection entered into force on 23 June 2026, after an 18-month grace period. It is enforced by the new Data Protection Authority (APDP). Cross-border transfers and foreign hosting require showing equivalent protection and prior authorisation. Declaration formalities for small businesses were not read in the text.

sources.title: CAMEROUN : La loi sur la protection des données à caractère personnel entre en vigueur ce 23 juin 2026
sources.quote: Promulguée en fin d'année 2024, la Loi n° 2024/017 avait accordé un moratoire de 18 mois aux entreprises et administrations publiques.

sources.quote: À l’approche de l’échéance fatidique du 23 juin 2026, la mise en conformité n’est plus une option mais une obligation pour éviter des sanctions lourdes de l’Autorité de protection des données à caractère Personnel (APDP).

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under Law 2010/021 on e-commerce, consumers may withdraw within 15 days, counted from the day after receipt for goods (art. 20). The seller must refund within 15 days of return or renunciation. Non-conforming or late goods may be returned within 15 days of delivery (art. 21). The framework consumer law 2011/012 separately grants up to 14 days for contracts concluded at the supplier's initiative (art. 7).

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: The IGS single tax for turnover up to FCFA 50m, which covers several taxes including VAT (L3), is the main simplification. No freelancer-specific incentive was found.
L7_incentives.note: No source on tax holidays/incentives for individuals found on 2026-10-21; IGS details are covered in L3.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: The national identity card (CNI). Its number is used for online NIU registration, and the NIU itself is required to open a bank account (L2).
D1_id_document.note: CNI role rests on NIU guides only; no ID-authority source captured on 2026-10-21.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed). The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
